Transvaalkwartier — The Hague, Netherlands

Relatively safer day Average night

In detail

Next to the Schilderswijk and named with it in most writing about The Hague's difficult neighbourhoods — writing that, as Dutch sources point out, comes largely from people who do not live in either. The Hague's own figures are published per wijk through Den Haag in Cijfers and the national Veiligheidsmonitor, a population survey run for CBS and the Ministry of Justice and Security. Dense nineteenth-century housing with documented drug and youth crime; residential, and not on any visitor's route.

Frequently asked questions

Is Transvaalkwartier safe?

Wandroz currently rates Transvaalkwartier in The Hague as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in The Hague during the day and roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in The Hague at night. This comes from a structured local-source assessment: an area-level review of credible local sources — local and national news, municipal and police-published material, and official surveys where they exist — consolidated across sources rather than taken from a single report. Is Transvaalkwartier safe at night?

At night, Transvaalkwartier is rated as roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in The Hague. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Transvaalkwartier a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Transvaalkwartier's day rating (relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in The Hague) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late.
